doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Norman Connors, Chet Baker, Ron Carter and Patrice Rushen dates
summary: Brown lists further 1974-75 sessions and Laws recalls few of them, mentioning dating Patrice Rushen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I’ve got a recording that you recorded there. But we’ll get back to that. Next, Slewfoot with Norman Connors. So he had already done his other major all-star session. Here’s the second one – another – probably the third one. Some of the same folks. I’m not sure if this was – this was recorded in July ’74, New York, Eddie Henderson, yourself, Gary Bartz, Lonnie Liston Smith, Dom Um Romao on percussion
Then Chet Baker, a session with Chet Baker at Rudy Van Gelder’s. Then here comes Ron Carter, Spanish Blue.
I don’t remember that. I remember the title, but I don’t – I just don’t remember the recording.
Then George Benson when he was at Carnegie Hall, under his name.
I heard those recordings, but I just – I was surprised to hear them, because I forgot I had done them.
How about Ron Carter’s Anything Goes?
Okay. Lennie White. It was just one session. Venusian Summer.
Then Patrice Rushen, Before the Dawn. We talked about Patrice, looked at her in the photo gallery.
Yeah, that was done up there at Fantasy Records. That was one of the times I was kind of dating her. We went to sushi. I remember that. Interesting.
